newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down after late selloff.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down after late selloff.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended lower Thursday in a fairly active session, hit by a late wave of technical selling when upside momentum stalled in the afternoon, trade sources said.

September slipped 4.4 cents to close at $2.428 per million British thermal units after stalling at $2.55. October settled 3.6 cents lower at $2.457. Most other deferreds ended steady to down three cents.

"When September dropped through unchanged, we hit some sell stops and then the pressure accelerated," said one Midwest trader, noting technical selling and long liquidation undermined the complex today.
While concerns about lagging storage should temper the bears, traders said the lack of weather support next week could keep the market on the defensive near-term.
In addition, they noted significant open interest in September with nine days left until expiry which could signal more long liquidation ahead.
Hub open interest on August 13 climbed 7,561 contracts to a record 223,148, with the bulk of the gain coming in October. September, which was down slightly, still has 44,569 lots open.

Technical traders pegged key September resistance at the contract high and double top at $2.605, with further selling likely at the $2.64-2.655 spot continuation chart gap from late January. Support was seen at $2.34 and $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.25-2.27.

In the cash Thursday, Gulf Coast prices jumped more than a a dime to the low-to-mid $2.50s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the low-to-mid $2.40s. New York city gate gas gained 10-15 cents to the low-to-mid $2.70s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip fell 2.7 cents to $2.335. NYMEX said 55,233 contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 64,841.

On the KCBT, September finished 5.5 cents lower at $2.34, while deferreds ended down by one to 3.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.1 cents to 8.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 368 lots traded, up from Wednesday's total of 241.
